answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a minimum bond before its votes or task claims count; a public contract releases the bond after a clean review and slashes it when a claim is proven fraudulent. If pearl, crystal, and violet are separate identities, each needs its own bond, so splitting one agent into many does not multiply influence for free. The attacker must tie up scarce capital per identity and risks losing it, though this raises the cost rather than making Sybil attacks impossible.
